articles.title: Small SaaS US/EU Image Thumbnails: Object Storage, CDN, or Resize on Upload?
articles.excerpt: Small SaaS US/EU Image Thumbnails: Object Storage, CDN, or Resize on Upload? Short answer: keep the original and generated thumbnails in tenant-scoped object storage, and resize on upload when the thu…
articles.body: Small SaaS US/EU Image Thumbnails: Object Storage, CDN, or Resize on Upload? Short answer: keep the original and generated thumbnails in tenant-scoped object storage, and resize on upload when the thumbnail sizes are known and stable; use an image CDN when sizes or transformations are still changing, and do not put large media bytes through the application server. That choice is less about image quality than about blast radius. A B2B SaaS serving customers in the US and EU needs a boring upload path, predictable storage keys, and a clear rule for who can read a thumbnail. The smallest architecture is the one that makes a tenant mix-up difficult to express.

articles.title: Find wasted Google Ads spend with n-gram analysis in Python
articles.excerpt: An n-gram, in a Google Ads context, is a word or short run of words that appears inside your search terms: "jobs", "near me" or "free template". Looking at search terms one by one hides patterns, beca…
articles.body: An n-gram, in a Google Ads context, is a word or short run of words that appears inside your search terms: "jobs", "near me" or "free template". Looking at search terms one by one hides patterns, because a wasteful word is usually spread across dozens of different searches, each too small to notice. Adding up cost and conversions by n-gram brings those patterns to the surface. This post builds a small pandas script that does exactly that from a standard search terms report export. No API access is needed: just a CSV and about sixty lines of Python. What you'll get Two CSV files: Waste candidates: n-grams with meaningful cost and no conversions. These are where negative keywords usually come from.

articles.body: Anyone can curve-fit a rational number to 137.036 in Python after peeking at CODATA. That is numerology, not physics—and it survives only because informal prose hides where experimental values leaked into the derivation. In Smithian Fold Theory (SFT V4) , I eliminated that escape hatch inside the Lean 4.35 kernel across 9,000+ modules and 55,000+ theorems . Every claim in the repository compiles with literally ZERO axioms : no Classical.choice , no propext , no Quot.sound , and zero native_decide . Running #print axioms on the top-level theorems returns an empty list, and even the SHA-256 integrity checks run purely inside the Lean kernel. articles.title: Auditing Legacy Web Projects to Spot Past Flaws, Gather Peer Lessons on Dropped Practices, and Curb Technical Debt
articles.excerpt: Retrospective Audit: Re-Examining Legacy Web Architectures When you open an old repository and wince at what you wrote two or three years ago, the discomfort usually points to a real structural flaw r…
articles.body: Retrospective Audit: Re-Examining Legacy Web Architectures When you open an old repository and wince at what you wrote two or three years ago, the discomfort usually points to a real structural flaw rather than bad taste. In software, friction accumulates mechanically: every extra layer of indirection increases the number of files, state transitions, and mental hops required for a single change to propagate. When a simple state update has to pass through a component lifecycle hook, a wrapper selector, an event bus, and a side-effect runner before mutating the DOM, each hop adds latency in developer comprehension and raises the odds that a stale reference or uncleaned subscription survives a refactor. Look closely at what actually breaks during a retrospective audit.

articles.title: The Ansible alternative you can actually migrate to
articles.excerpt: Ansible has many shortcomings, but until now there has not been an alternative that is simple to migrate to. Ansible alternatives such as Puppet, Salt and Chef are structurally different from Ansible,…
articles.body: Ansible has many shortcomings, but until now there has not been an alternative that is simple to migrate to. Ansible alternatives such as Puppet, Salt and Chef are structurally different from Ansible, which is a barrier to migration: nobody ports an Ansible playbook to Puppet, they rewrite it against a different model of the world. Reemote is a Python configuration-management library that is very similar to Ansible. Reemote is so similar to Ansible that it is possible to migrate existing Ansible roles into Python. What Ansible is bad at, and what Python gives back Ansible's shortcomings mostly follow from one decision: configuration is written in a data-serialization format with a templating dialect bolted on, rather than in a programming language.

articles.excerpt: The Richat Structure, also known as the “Eye of the Sahara,” is seen from the International Space Station as it orbited above on Nov. 14, 2026. It is an eroded geological dome about 100 million years…
articles.body: NASA/Luke Delaney The Richat Structure, also known as the “Eye of the Sahara,” is seen from the International Space Station as it orbited above on Nov. 14, 2026. It is an eroded geological dome about 100 million years old created by igneous activity and uplift in the nation of Mauritania. In this type of geologic structure, rocks exposed in the center of the “bullseye” are older than rocks forming the outer rings. This structure measures 45 kilometers (28 miles) across and is made up of igneous and sedimentary rocks. Image credit: NASA/Luke Delaney

Its destination is the Didymos-Dimorphos asteroid system, which consists of the larger Didymos , a " rubble pile" asteroid , and its smaller moonlet Dimorphos. NASA slammed a kinetic impactor into Dimorphos in 2022 in the historic DART test , which confirmed that such an impact can alter the trajectory of an asteroid. Hera arrives at Didymos today, and ESA is sharing the first close-up images from the mission in a free online livestream. ESA's livestream starts at 1:45 p.m.

articles.title: Astronomers discover the most distant and ancient supermassive black hole-powered quasar in the universe
articles.excerpt: The Euclid space telescope has spotted the most distant and ancient quasar ever seen, a bright cosmic event powered by a supermassive black hole with 360 million times the mass of the sun.
articles.body: The Euclid space telescope has spotted the most distant and ancient quasar ever seen, a bright cosmic event powered by a supermassive black hole with 360 million times the mass of the sun. The supermassive black hole is seen as it was just 630 million years after the Big Bang. 40 million years further back in time than the previous record holder for the most ancient quasar. The discovery further deepens the mystery of how supermassive black holes grew so massive so soon into the history of the universe. That's because previously, scientists had theorized it should take 1 billion years of feeding and merging for black holes to reach supermassive status of millions or billions of times as massive as the sun.
